name: forge-2.0 rate model
about: The benchmark's own Jira rate world. Atlassian publishes no per-endpoint costs; the dev and scoring sites charge exactly this. Times are virtual (FORGE2-CONTRACT.md §11).

quota.reset: at the top of each virtual hour; nothing carries over
quota.wall: hard: once the hour's points are spent, every request is answered 429 until the reset
quota.why: the app's fair share of its 65,000-point Tier 1 hourly pool, which every tenant of the app shares (about 27 tenants)

background.rule: background requests may use at most 70 % of any virtual hour's quota (the admin setting Background share (%) moves this limit, 10-90)

is: resolvers invoked from a UI surface (Custom UI or UI Kit)
personFacing.rule: a person-facing request is never refused for quota

costs.counting: every started block of 50 counts: 0 issues = 1 point, 1-50 = 2, 51-100 = 3
every started block of 50 counts: 1-50 updates = 2 points, 51-100 = 3

costs.request: any other POST, PUT or DELETE

burst.bucket: one token bucket per endpoint: method + path template (for example GET /rest/api/3/issue/{issueIdOrKey})
burst.rule: a request draws its points from its endpoint's bucket; a request the bucket cannot pay for is answered 429 jira-burst-based

perIssueWrites.rule: at most 1 write per issue per 2 s; another write to the same issue inside the window is answered 429 jira-per-issue-on-write

nearLimit.when: fewer than 20 % of the hour's points (480) remain

reasons.jira-quota-tenant-based: the hour's quota is spent; Retry-After = seconds to the next virtual hour
reasons.jira-burst-based: the endpoint's burst bucket is empty
reasons.jira-per-issue-on-write: a second write to one issue inside its 2 s window

reactions.jira-quota-tenant-based: pause ALL background requests until the reset
reactions.jira-per-issue-on-write: delay writes to that issue only
reactions.always: never send the next attempt before Retry-After has passed
